concepts.name: Counseling Agency Registry
concepts.summary: Spring Boot service managing counseling agencies (Beratungsstellen) for the platform: agency master data, addresses, settings, and public agency lookup used during asker registration. Agencies belong to a Träger (tenant) and carry per-agency feature settings served to the counselling app.

concepts.name: Agency Administration
concepts.summary: AgencyAdminController plus AgencyAdminService cover the admin-facing lifecycle: creating, updating, and configuring agencies, topic assignment, admin controls, postcode ranges, and the ADR-014 legal-text library endpoints. The admin OpenAPI contract (agencyadminservice.yaml) grew substantially in July/August 2026 with agency-ID allocation, legal-text CRUD, and department legal endpoints.

concepts.name: Agency Search & Matching
concepts.summary: Public agency search resolves the right agency for an asker (postcode/topic-based matching) before registration completes. Since #194/#196 the topic aggregation only reports topics a help-seeker can actually reach (reachability filter in AgencyRepository), so offline/hidden agencies no longer leak topics into registration.

concepts.name: Department Legal Texts (ADR-003 / ADR-014)
concepts.summary: A department (Fachbereich = agency x topic, AgencyTopic entity) carries a data privacy policy (DPP) and imprint. ADR-014 adds a tenant-owned reusable LegalText library: several departments may share one text per kind, or fall back to their inline content. Content is a JSON language-to-HTML map, OWASP-sanitised by LegalContentSanitizer. Publishing a department-specific edit breaks the shared link (#193); agencies also got agency-level legal texts the inheritance chain assumed (#222, changeset 0027). Only PUBLISHED texts are served to end users via the unauthenticated read side.

concepts.name: Agency ID Allocation (TEN-INV-U2)
concepts.summary: Collision-free, DB-arbitrated allocation of agency IDs for the tenant-invite flow (parent ORISO-Admin#569). IDs are FREE, RESERVED (open invite holds a row in agency_id_reservation, PK = the ID) or ASSIGNED (agency row, never re-issued, soft-deleted included). Assignment checks run as native SQL so a tenant-scoped admin's Hibernate tenant filter can never hide another Träger's agency and report a taken ID as free. Concurrency safety comes from the primary key and write-then-read transactions, not app-level checks.

concepts.name: Effective Permission Settings (ADR-013 P4)
concepts.summary: AgencyEffectivePermissionSettingsApplier applies upper-role permission constraints (AgencyAdminControls) to the public feature flags served to the counselling app: allowed=false forces a feature off, enforced=true forces it on, otherwise the agency's own setting stands (#297). Mirrors TenantService's applier at agency level; the server is the single source of truth and the raw controls are never attached to the public agency response. Agency settings also mirror the media flag families (upload / inline display / AI scan, per chat type) from the media epic; the old attachment flag is retired.

concepts.name: Multitenancy & Cross-Träger Isolation
concepts.summary: Tenant resolution chain (access token, custom header, subdomain, technical user) feeds TenantContext; TenantAspect enables the Hibernate tenant filter on tenant-aware repositories so one Träger's admins cannot see another's agencies. Agency admins without a domain user claim are tolerated since #143. Deliberate escape hatches (tenant-unaware repository, native-SQL checks in ID allocation) exist where global uniqueness matters.

concepts.name: Matrix Agency Provisioning
concepts.summary: Each agency gets a Matrix bot/user provisioned via the Synapse admin API (MatrixProvisioningService). Since AS-C01 the per-agency Matrix passwords are encrypted at rest (AgencyMatrixPasswordCipher, AES) and the internal credentials endpoint is protected. Rocket.Chat configuration and its residual environment contract were fully removed (#191); the service is Matrix-only and CI attests Matrix-only images.

concepts.name: Agency Deletion & Purge Workflow
concepts.summary: Cron-driven delete workflow: agencies flagged deleted are purged in batch, but since #202 each agency purges inside its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction (AgencyPurgeTransaction) so one failure no longer takes the whole batch down and gets a per-agency log line. Departments (agency_topic) are removed via JPA cascade/orphanRemoval, an explicit redundant delete was dropped (#220); postcode ranges need the explicit delete.

concepts.name: Admin Agency List Sorting
concepts.summary: GET /agencyadmin/agencies supports whitelist-based sorting via the generated Sort.FieldEnum; SortParameterBindingConfig binds the admin frontend's upper-cased separator-free field names (POSTCODE, CREATEDATE) leniently onto the underscore enum constants instead of rejecting them with HTTP 400 (Admin#308 / AS#128 package). The enum acts as the sort-field whitelist.

flows.name: Agency Lookup During Registration
flows.summary: Asker enters registration context -> public agency search (AgencyController) matches by postcode/consulting type/topic, reporting only reachable topics -> effective permission settings are applied server-side to the returned feature flags -> selected agency determines the consulting setup downstream.

flows.name: Legal Text Authoring to Public Read
flows.summary: Tenant admin authors a reusable LegalText (or inline department text) -> LegalContentSanitizer cleans multilingual HTML -> text is assigned to departments; publishing a department-specific edit breaks the shared link -> once PUBLISHED, end users read it unauthenticated via /agencies/{agencyId}/topics/{topicId}/legal (DepartmentLegalService); drafts never reach clients.

flows.name: Agency ID Reservation and Creation
flows.summary: Admin invite flow checks /agencyadmin/agencyids/{id}/availability or asks for next-free -> reservation row inserted (PK arbitration, write-then-read) -> agency creation guards against open reservations inside its insert transaction -> IDs are never re-issued, even for soft-deleted agencies.

flows.name: Scheduled Agency Purge
flows.summary: agency.deleteworkflow.cron triggers DeleteAgencyService -> each deleted-flagged agency is purged in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction (AgencyPurgeTransaction) -> postcode ranges deleted explicitly, departments cascade via JPA -> failures are isolated and logged per agency.
